title: The Customer Friction Playbook
summary: Find where effort, uncertainty or delay gets in the way of your customers, then decide which barriers deserve attention first.
coverAlt: Typographic website edition of The Customer Friction Playbook cover
searchText: the customer friction playbook a practical system for finding, prioritising and fixing the barriers that stop customers from buying, staying and returning find where effort, uncertainty or delay gets in the way of your customers, then decide which barriers deserve attention first. every customer journey involves a sequence of decisions and actions. this playbook focuses on understanding where those actions become unnecessarily difficult and what a business can do about it. work through a structured improvement sequence: map, detect, diagnose, prioritise, redesign and measure. keep the focus on the cause of a problem and the evidence needed to assess the result. customer experience customer journey business improvement customer friction customer retention

title: The Missed Revenue Playbook
summary: Examine opportunities within your existing business and evaluate what may be recoverable, what it would cost to act and what evidence would demonstrate a worthwhile result.
coverAlt: Typographic website edition of The Missed Revenue Playbook cover
searchText: the missed revenue playbook how to find, evaluate and recover revenue your business is already positioned to capture examine opportunities within your existing business and evaluate what may be recoverable, what it would cost to act and what evidence would demonstrate a worthwhile result. revenue opportunities deserve careful evaluation. this playbook explores how to examine opportunities a business may already be positioned to capture, while considering costs, operational demands and customer impact. an opportunity estimate is not a verified result. keep baseline performance, attribution, incremental effect and contribution in view when assessing what an improvement actually achieves. revenue opportunities revenue evaluation business improvement missed revenue revenue opportunities

searchText: the business playbook series practical frameworks for business improvement. each playbook examines a distinct business challenge, helping owners and teams investigate what is happening and decide where to focus.

title: Four questions before you change a business process
summary: A short reflection for turning a business observation into an investigation.
searchText: four questions before you change a business process a short reflection for turning a business observation into an investigation. what did you actually observe? describe the specific event or repeated pattern. separate what you saw from your explanation of why it happened. who experienced the problem, and at which step? place the observation in a customer or operational journey. avoid assuming every customer has the same experience. what evidence could challenge your explanation? look for exceptions, alternative causes and missing information before choosing a solution. how would you check the effect of a change? decide what to measure, over what period and against which baseline. consider cost and unintended consequences alongside the intended benefit. business improvement evidence decision making

title: The business reflection worksheet
summary: A free, simple worksheet to record one observation, the evidence you have and what you still need to check.
searchText: the business reflection worksheet a free, simple worksheet to record one observation, the evidence you have and what you still need to check. choose one customer or revenue question in your business. record the observation first, then identify the evidence you need before deciding what to do. this introductory worksheet is an original website resource. it is not a chapter excerpt or a validated business assessment. business improvement worksheet
